title: Restoration
definition: Restoration is God's gracious work of bringing repentant people back into renewed fellowship, obedience, usefulness, and hope.
summary: Restoration shows that failure does not have to be the final word when there is repentance and grace.
christFocus: Jesus restores fallen people through mercy, truth, repentance, and renewed calling.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Restoration is a deeply biblical theme. God does not minimize sin, but He also does not despise a broken and contrite heart. Through repentance and grace, He restores people to fellowship and renewed obedience.

Restoration is not pretending sin never happened. It involves honesty, confession, forgiveness, accountability, healing, and often patient rebuilding of trust. But it holds out hope that God can renew what sin has damaged.

In the Church, restoration should be handled with truth and gentleness. The goal is not to permanently mark people by their worst failure but to help them return to faithful life in Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people believe failure disqualifies them forever from God's care or usefulness. Restoration matters because it proclaims that Christ is able to forgive, heal, renew, and recommission repentant sinners.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring failure into the light before God. Seek repentance, wise accountability, and practical obedience. When restoring others, hold truth and mercy together, remembering how Christ has shown mercy to you.
